Try $k=3$?
With 4 nodes, max number of disjoint edges is 2. But transitive links create more pairs.
If A uses $(1,2), (2,3), (3,4)$, then $1 \to 2, 2 \to 3, 3 \to 4$ and transitively $1 \to 3, 2 \to 4, 1 \to 4$.
$R_A$ contains all pairs $(i,j)$ with $i<j$.
Then $R_A \cap R_B$ will definitely be non-empty unless $R_B$ is empty, which is impossible if $k \ge 1$.
So if one company creates a Hamiltonian path, intersection is guaranteed.
